# Asaṅkhata Saṁyutta (SN 43)

**ID:** SN 43
**Section:** Saṁyuttanikāya (sn)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-1
**Title (Pali):** Asaṅkhata Saṁyutta
**Title (English, SuttaCentral):** Linked Discourses on the Unconditioned
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/sn43
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0304m.mul8.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Asaṅkhatasaṁyutta* (SN 43) is the forty-third collection of the *Saṁyuttanikāya*, situated toward the end of the *Saḷāyatanavagga* (PTS SN iv 359–373) [Bodhi 2003; Norman 1983]. It serves as a comprehensive compendium describing the unconditioned (*asaṅkhata*)—the third noble truth, identified with *nibbāna* and defined as the destruction of lust, hatred, and delusion (*rāgakkhayo dosakkhayo mohakkhayo*)—alongside the practical paths that lead to its realization [Bodhi 2003; Yinshun; SuttaCentral]. The collection is divided into two sections (*vagga*): the first (*paṭhamo vaggo*, SN 43.1–11) details eleven presentations of the path, opening with mindfulness directed to the body (*kāyagatāsati*) and various samādhi practices, while the second vagga expands these presentations across forty-five path factors combined with dozens of epithets for the goal (such as *amata*, *santa*, and *saraṇa*), mostly condensed by repetitive abbreviation [Bodhi 2003; Norman 1983; Dhivan and Sagaraghosa 2011]. The discourses conclude with the Buddha's admonition to practice meditation (*jhāyatha*) in secluded places and not be negligent [Polak 2011].

In the Chinese translation of the *Saṁyuktāgama*, the counterpart *Asaṅkhatasaṁyutta* is positioned toward the end of the *Maggavagga* (*Mahāvagga*) rather than the *Saḷāyatanavagga*, highlighting the realization of the unconditioned as the fruit of spiritual practice [Bodhi 2003]. SuttaCentral lists SĀ 890 (無為法) as the principal parallel to SN 43.11–43 [SuttaCentral]. Comparative analysis reveals differences in content; for instance, SN 43.4 lists the threefold concentration of emptiness (*suññata*), the signless (*animitta*), and the desireless or undirected (*appaṇihita*), an enumeration absent in SĀ 890 [Yinshun; Choong 1999]. DharmaNexus records massive internal Pali text-sharing—most heavily with the *Magga Saṁyutta* (SN 45), *Bojjhaṅga Saṁyutta* (SN 46), and *Catukkanipāta* (AN 4)—as well as cross-language alignments with canonical and scholastic treatises such as the Tibetan *Abhidharmakośaṭīkopayikā* (D4094) and Sanskrit *Arthaviniścayasūtra* [DharmaNexus].
